---
title: "Custom model design"
---

An annotation is an observed response produced by a measurement procedure. It is not the linguistic property that the procedure is meant to inform. The measurement procedure connects a linguistic unit, a prompt, an annotator, a response scale, and the recorded answer. A custom likelihood should encode those parts without turning a response into direct access to the target property.

This module uses two annotation resources, one of them non-English. The natural-parts task in [Universal Decompositional Semantics (UDS)](https://aclanthology.org/2020.lrec-1.699/) records binary answers about predicate nodes in English dependency graphs; [Gantt, Glass, and White (2022)](https://aclanthology.org/2022.tacl-1.2/) describe the event-structure protocol. The course extract is pinned to the official [`decomp` 0.3.2 release](https://pypi.org/project/decomp/0.3.2/): the data are CC BY-SA 4.0, while the toolkit code is MIT-licensed. The [ITU/IMST Turkish PropBank](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-017-9390-y) records worker selections among predicate-specific role descriptions, followed by aggregation and adjudication; the [project release](https://turkishpropbank.github.io/) supplies the source data and guidelines.

The Turkish PropBank project site applies CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 to resources built in the project, while the repository's short license header names the Turkish frame files specifically. The course extract follows the project-wide noncommercial statement, but the narrower repository header should not be read as a separate license grant for every crowd export.

```{r}
#| label: custom-model-index
#| message: false
#| warning: false

uds <- read.csv(
  "data/uds/uds-natural-parts.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
turkish <- read.csv(
  "data/turkish-propbank/role-agreement-judgments.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

measurement_inventory <- data.frame(
  resource = c(
    "UDS natural-parts responses",
    "UDS predicate-node items",
    "Turkish PropBank judgments",
    "Turkish PropBank argument-candidate items"
  ),
  count = c(
    nrow(uds),
    length(unique(uds$item_id)),
    nrow(turkish),
    length(unique(turkish$item_id))
  )
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(uds) == 2955L,
  length(unique(uds$item_id)) == 1000L,
  length(unique(uds$annotator_id)) == 12L,
  nrow(turkish) == 55207L,
  length(unique(turkish$item_id)) == 18306L,
  length(unique(turkish$worker_id)) == 144L
)

measurement_inventory
```

The two response variables answer different questions. UDS records whether an annotator answered yes to one natural-parts gate. Turkish PropBank records whether an individual role-description selection agrees with the project's adjudication. Neither response is an independently observed linguistic truth.

## From the protocol to a probability model

[A data-generating process](generative-stories.qmd) first specifies the random steps that could produce the UDS gate responses. [Writing a joint model](writing-a-joint-model.qmd) then translates those steps into a joint probability distribution over the observed item--annotator pairs. [Parameter recovery](parameter-recovery.qmd) asks whether the complete procedure can recover known values under the released incidence design.

The Turkish PropBank analysis next treats [annotations as measurements](annotations-as-measurements.qmd), distinguishing agreement with adjudication from label validity or worker competence. Returning to UDS, [annotator effects](annotator-effects.qmd) represent stable response-location differences among annotators.

The [UDS measurement-model capstone](uds-measurement-model.qmd) combines the likelihood, priors, parameter-recovery study, partial pooling, posterior summaries, and posterior predictive checks. Finally, [gated annotations](gated-annotations.qmd) retains the protocol's symbolic gate-and-branch factorization while using only the observed natural-parts gate numerically. The raw confidence field and conditional follow-up branches remain outside the empirical model because their representation could not be verified against the paper and release.

## What the sequence supports

The UDS item is a predicate node anchored in sentence context, not a context-free verb lemma. The Turkish PropBank item is one predicate-specific argument candidate, not an abstract thematic-role type. Keeping those units distinct fixes the product terms in the likelihood and the populations represented by the random effects.

These joint models depend on previously introduced [response distributions](../regression-models/generalized-linear-models.qmd), [grouped variation](../regression-models/random-effects.qmd), [posterior computation](../statistical-inference/markov-chain-monte-carlo.qmd), and [posterior predictive checks](../statistical-inference/posterior-predictive-checks.qmd). The sequence contributes the protocol-specific joint distribution and the checks needed to interpret its latent quantities.
